To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HER-2 overexpressing cells are resistant to the aromataser inhibitor letrozole.

HER-2 over-expression in breast cancer cells leads to increased estrogen receptor activity, increased estrogen-responsive gene expression and cell proliferation, and resistance to aromatase inhibition.

HER-2 overexpressing MCF-7 cells are resistant to the antiestrogenic effects of letrozole and that this resistance is due to ligand-independent recruitment and/or increased recruitment of AIB1/CBP coactivator complexes by ER.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of HER-2 in the development of aromatase inhibitor resistance in breast cancer.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies to overcome endocrine resistance in breast cancer.

elucidating the molecular mechanism(s) of resistance to aromatase inhibitors in breast cancer cells and how this may be related to the development of breast tumors with a poor prognosis and/or resistance to chemotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HER2 gene is not a predictive marker of response to aromatase inhibitor treatment.
HER-2 over-expression in MCF- 7/CA breast cancer cells confers resistance to the aromase inhibitor letrozol.
the HER-2 receptor plays a key role in the development and maintenance of aromatase inhibitor resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aromatase overexpressing cells with HER-2 overexpressing are more resistant to aromatase inhibitor than the control aromatase overexpression cells.
HER-2 over expression can lead to resistance to aromatase inhibitor therapy by increasing ER transcriptional activity in the presence or absence of estrogen.
the overexpression of HER-2 is associated with aromatase inhibitor resistance in breast cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HER2 overexpression in breast cancer can lead to a loss of sensitivity to aromatase inhibitor therapy.
HER2 overexpression can lead to letrozole resistance in ER+ breast cancer cells by increasing the activity of the estrogen receptor.
HER-2 amplification or overexpression can lead to aromatase inhibitor resistance.
